body: The listing does not name a single plant in this formula, so this page does not name one either. What it does print is the serving: two capsules a day with at least 500 ml of water.
If you want the list before you buy, ring the shop and somebody will go and read you what is written on the sack.
Two capsules a day, with at least 500 ml of water.

The listing gives no time of day. Two a day is the printed serving. The listing prints no maximum; the statutory line at the foot of this page is where do not exceed the stated dose comes from. If you miss a day, take two the next day rather than four.
Not printed on the listing. Dry, out of direct sun and lid on is what we would do with any capsule, and a capsule needs no fridge.
Not for children. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or you take prescribed medication, ask your GP or pharmacist before you start.
An unprinted ingredient list cannot be checked against a prescription by anybody, including us. That is a reason to ask first rather than to assume.
Sent out from 599 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, Tuesday to Sunday. UK delivery is free over £50, or you can collect from the shop between 10 and 6, any day except Monday.

ingredients.intro: Nothing, is the short answer. The listing for this jar names no plant, no part of a plant and no amount, so there is no ingredient card here with a species on it. The frames below are left empty rather than filled with a plant we have guessed at from the name on the front. If you want the list before you buy, ask at the counter and somebody will go and look at the sack.

cards.p: The listing prints no ingredients at all for this formula. We are not going to reconstruct one from the product name, from the tags on the shop, or from what a formula of this kind usually contains. An invented list is worse than a blank one.

rows: Not printed. The listing does not name a single ingredient in this formula.
Nutropic is the product name and nothing else on this page. We do not say what the formula is for, because we are not permitted to and would not guess.

This is not a replacement for anything a doctor has prescribed, which is the listing's own line. Nothing here is a reason to stop or change prescribed treatment.
spec.smallprint: Do not exceed the stated dose. Speak to your GP or pharmacist before starting any supplement, particularly if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or take medication. Food supplements should not be used as a substitute for a varied and balanced diet and a healthy lifestyle. Keep out of reach of young children.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: This is the thinnest sheet on the site. Most of the rows say not printed, and that is the state of this jar today rather than a house habit. What the formula is for is not on this page, and neither is the list of what is in it, because the listing does not give us one to print.

reiss.label: From Reiss
paras: A jar that does not print its ingredients is a jar nobody can check. Not your GP, not the pharmacist reading your repeat prescription, and not me at the counter with the tub in my hand. That is the whole of my objection to it, and it is why the sheet above says not printed in row after row instead of filling the gaps with something plausible.

The word on the front is a name. It is not a description and it is not a promise, and this page does not translate it into one. If you want to know what you are swallowing, the ingredient list is the only thing that answers that question, and it is not printed yet.

If the list gets printed, it goes here in full: every plant in Latin, the part of it used, in the order the label declares them, the way the Decolonise sheet does it. Until then the page stays thin and the tub stays on the shelf for people who already know what they are buying and have asked.
reiss.pull: A jar that will not print its ingredients is a jar nobody can check.
